SELECTED_MODEL.name: Llama-3.2-3B
SELECTED_MODEL.why: only candidate that runs in the FROZEN environment with zero dependency changes, so the Llama-2-7B arm stays bit-reproducible and the model axis is the only thing that moves. Different generation (2023 Llama-2 vs 2024 Llama-3.2), different tokenizer (32k vs 128k vocab), different scale (7B vs 3B) — enough to test whether the double reversal is a Llama-2-7B pathology. It is also the model the neighbouring Critical Look study used for its additional-model BBH experiments, so the comparison is natural.
SELECTED_MODEL.caveat: same Llama family, so it is a weaker generality test than a cross-family model would be. This must be stated as a limitation rather than glossed.

cost_estimate.warm_up_checkpoint: ~1.5 h (must be rebuilt: warm-up is model-specific)
cost_estimate.candidate_gradient_datastore: ~6-8 h for 270,679 candidates at proj_dim 8192 — the dominant cost; MUST be rebuilt because the central claim is about model-specific gradient geometry
cost_estimate.selections_DSMC_First_RR_Second_RR: ~1.5 h (Random-K reuses the frozen candidate indices)
cost_estimate.evaluation_25_runs: 24 adapters + 1 no-SFT reference, ~60-70 min each at 3B => ~26-29 h

must_not_do: do NOT train the second model on Llama-2-selected subsets and call it replication — that is cross-model transfer of Llama-2 selections, a different scientific question. The new model rebuilds its own warm-up, candidate gradients, target gradients and target-aware selections. Random-K DOES reuse the same frozen candidate indices so the model axis stays clean.
no_accuracy_used: no BBH accuracy or SFT result informed this choice
